lede: The biggest thing this week is Tuesday's BOCC meeting, where the county votes on two Land Use Code amendments — one updating rules for natural medicine businesses and one reshaping how nonconforming lots are treated, the kind of quiet code language that has real consequences for what gets built where. Also on Tuesday, San Miguel County holds its sixth working session on rewriting housing code to make workforce and affordable housing easier to build. On Wednesday, HARC takes up the Carhenge redevelopment at 700 W Pacific Ave — three large-scale public hearings on a multi-building project that will define what that corner of town looks like for a long time.
